Detailed Summary:
Sarah Olson, a 75-year-old female, was seen on September 13, 2024, for a follow-up on her chronic pancreatitis. She reports feeling well overall, though she continues to experience occasional mild abdominal discomfort. The patient’s chronic pancreatitis, which began in November 2011, is attributed to alcohol use and remains controlled without the need for current medication. Her vital signs on this visit were as follows: blood pressure 166/89 mmHg and weight 167 lbs.

During the December 25, 2023, encounter, Sarah was seen for a routine lab review. She reported no significant new symptoms. Her blood pressure was recorded at 168/95 mmHg, and her weight was 165 lbs. Laboratory results from this visit were within normal limits, and her pancreatitis remained stable.

On April 6, 2023, Sarah presented for a follow-up related to her pancreatitis. She again noted mild, intermittent abdominal pain. Her vital signs included a blood pressure of 160/87 mmHg and a weight of 176 lbs. Her chronic pancreatitis was noted to be controlled without the need for any medication changes. She continues to abstain from heavy alcohol consumption, maintaining an intake of approximately 4 drinks per week.

The July 16, 2022, visit was also for pancreatitis management. She reported feeling fairly well with controlled symptoms. Her blood pressure was 154/89 mmHg, and her weight was 174 lbs. Laboratory evaluations confirmed her pancreatitis remained under control. Sarah's social history reveals a moderate alcohol intake, with approximately 4 drinks per week.

Overall, Sarah Olson’s condition remains stable with her chronic pancreatitis effectively managed. Her blood pressure is consistently elevated, and she has experienced some fluctuations in her weight, currently at 167 lbs. There are no new concerning symptoms reported. Continued monitoring and adherence to her management are recommended.
